title: Lesson 01 page shape: orientation, claims, focus policy, running example, exit before extras
description: For chapters with structured claims. Orientation band of two columns (This lesson answers / By the end); position line 'Lesson 1 of 7 · The stack' above the headline (keep the chapter-kicker element). Claims strip: the claim is the primary interaction; selected state gets a subtle background and a '1 / 3' indicator; 'How we know' opens the drawer on the evidence component. Map policy: local toggle labelled 'Lesson focus | Explore map'. In Lesson focus, focused components at full weight, others receded (~45% opacity, still clickable, affordance on hover only); boundaries never recede; the Inspect affordance shows only on the evidence component. In Explore map, every component shows the affordance. Running example subordinated: collapsed to one line 'Running example: Follow a partition lookup →' that expands to the hops; selecting a hop enters trace (path up to that hop at full weight) and opens the drawer. Below the map: easy mistake as a left rule (no box), What you can now say (the same three claims), Next link, then a dashed rule and 'Optional · go deeper' with cue chips, field-guide previews (title + one line, expand in place), sources and scope note. Remove the exploration frame shadow. All state that is already in the URL stays in the URL; the selected claim may be local state.
acceptance_criteria: Visual match to the prototype at 1440px and 390px; keyboard: Tab order claims → toggle → map → drawer; browser back/forward and reload keep chapter, step, and detail; the other six lessons render unchanged apart from the drawer.

title: Contextual evidence drawer replaces the inspector column
description: Global for all map chapters. Closed on load (no default selection from scene.selected). Opens on component click, running-example hop, claim evidence link, easy-mistake map jump, or a route carrying ?detail=. Slides over the map at desktop width (map takes full width); the phone bottom sheet stays. Template in fixed order: Inspecting (node title), Owned by (detail.label), What it is (node subtitle), Why it matters here (detail.title + first sentence of body; rest behind a More disclosure), Verify it (artifact), Go deeper (source). Keep the seam's lock/pod state repeat at the top. Close with x or Escape; focus moves into the drawer on open and back to the opener on close.
acceptance_criteria: Every map chapter loads with the drawer closed; ?detail= deep links open it; Escape closes and refocuses; seam state repeat still present; phone sheet unchanged in behaviour.
notes: Codex (gpt-6-astra) implemented; could not commit or screenshot from its sandbox. Orchestrator verified visually at 1440 and 390. Review found 10 findings (2 high: stale trace after Back, drawer clipped on tall maps); fixes delegated to a Fable agent. title: Lesson 03 in the frozen grammar, with the cache-down trace
description: Express lesson 03 (the SPI boundary) in lesson 01's grammar. Claims: (1) Common service code calls a provider interface; the Azure implementation behind it does the Azure work with Workload Identity; for the partition service that is a cache, then a Table Storage read, and the read still happens when the cache throws: focus core, contract, azureimpl, azureclients, evidence azureimpl. (2) The interface and its implementation ship in one image; no network hop between them: focus contract, azureimpl, image, evidence image. (3) Upstream may delete its Azure implementations; the fork owns provider/<svc>-azure outside the generated upstream tree: focus upstream, azureimpl, engineering, evidence upstream. Add the cache-down trace as a variant of the running example: the same five hops with a switch that makes the fourth throw and the fifth answer anyway (a trace variant, not a second diagram). The Azure implementation's drawer entry links the real fix (commit fc2dfbf) as Go deeper with the ownership ADR second. Candidate headline: The provider lives inside the service. Litmus: point to where shared OSDU code ends and Azure provider code begins, with the drawer closed; the cache-throw fact must be on the page, not only in the drawer.
acceptance_criteria: Claims render with headlines under twelve words; cache-down trace selectable from the example strip and visible on the map; litmus answerable with the drawer closed; npm run check green; second-agent review before push to main.

SCOPE: src/content/chapters.js (the boundary lesson entry), src/content/component-details.js (the Azure implementation entry gains the fc2dfbf fix as Go deeper), src/components/pages.js, src/main.js, src/styles/pages.css, tests/content.test.js, docs/. title: Lesson 02 in the frozen grammar: moments as claims
description: Express lesson 02 (bring-up) in lesson 01's grammar as the first test of it. Claims (from today's outcomes, unchanged in substance): (1) The CLI and Bicep create Azure and seed the cluster; Flux assembles the workloads; controllers keep them healthy: moment Create Azure to Assemble OSDU, focus workstation, aks, bootstrap, flux, evidence flux. (2) A successful spi up exit is the first of five milestones, not readiness; spi status --watch follows the rest: moment Use the stack, focus readiness, initialization, caller, evidence readiness. (3) spi down removes compute and data but keeps identities and the resource group: moment Remove the stack, focus retained, evidence retained. Each claim gets a headline under twelve words, its full sentence, a why, focus, scopes, evidence, crossing. Selecting a claim selects its moment; the six moments stay the sequence control. The per-moment auto-open detail becomes a Look closer line. Candidate headline: One command creates the environment. Flux finishes it. Litmus: after it, can you explain how the stack gets created, with the drawer closed.
acceptance_criteria: Claims render with headlines; selecting a claim moves the moment and focuses the map; drawer closed by default; easy mistake then What you can now say then Next; npm run check green; second-agent review before push to main.

title: Round 4 tunes: short claim headlines, quiet rail, drawer content rule
description: Reviewer round 4 (13 Sep 2026): claim headlines were paragraph-like; inactive rail lessons carried subtitles; the drawer invariant needed to be a review rule. Done on main in 4b7ed98: claims gain a headline field rendered as the control label with the reason underneath (the full sentence still feeds What you can now say); rail subtitles show only on the current lesson; AGENTS.md carries the lesson grammar, the two-to-four claim range, and the rule that nothing required for What you can now say lives only in the drawer. Tests assert headline length and claim count.

title: Interaction hierarchy for Learn: claim is primary, everything else is evidence
description: Decided 13 September 2026 from the reviewer's third round. In a lesson: the claim is the primary interaction and changes the map; 'How we know' opens the drawer on the best evidence item; hops are subordinate and collapsed until asked; only the evidence component advertises Inspect in Lesson focus; receded components stay clickable with the affordance on hover; boundaries never recede. Local toggle is 'Lesson focus | Explore map' to avoid two levels of the word Explore. Deep links with ?detail= open the drawer. The drawer is a contextual evidence drawer, not a sidebar: it appears because the learner asked and then goes away. Headlines are the sentence to remember; the lesson name lives in the rail and position line. 'Listen to this lesson' waits for a per-lesson narration recorded from the claims; until then the cue row is labelled 'Hear it explained' in the optional band.
notes: Round 4 (13 Sep 2026) added: the lesson grammar is frozen as the standard (see AGENTS.md); claims carry a short headline as the control and the full sentence as the carry-forward line; two to four claims per lesson, count set by content; the review rule is that nothing required for What you can now say lives only in the drawer, and details answering how to prove, check, or debug belong in the drawer; navigation stays as is (LEARN rail plus Explore · Listen · Field guides); the book labels stay as quiet labels; the Easy mistake to What you can now say sequence is standard in every lesson.

title: Pilot lesson 01 with 4–5 engineers who know OSDU and not Azure SPI
description: Three questions, watched, no scores: (1) Without clicking anything, what are the three things this lesson is trying to teach you? (2) After using the claims, can you explain what the map is showing without opening the inspector? (3) When you click How we know, does the drawer feel like useful evidence or like you left the lesson? Record where they stop and which labels they misread. Decide from the answers whether to propagate the shape (epic D) or adjust it first.
acceptance_criteria: Notes filed as a dated doc in docs/; go/no-go recorded on the roll-out epic.
notes: Round 4: the pilot no longer gates lessons 02 and 03; it gates 04 to 06 and any navigation change. Run it in parallel with the 02/03 work.

title: Roll the lesson shape to 02–06 and unify the evidence component
description: Reviewer round 4 (13 Sep 2026) froze lesson 01's grammar: position line, headline, question and goal, two to four claims, one claim-focused map, optional evidence in the drawer, one easy mistake, What you can now say, next-lesson bridge, optional band. Lessons 02 and 03 are the test of that grammar and no longer wait for the pilot; 04, 05, 06 follow once 02 and 03 express cleanly and the pilot has run. Per lesson: outcomes become claims with headline, text, why, focus, scopes, evidence, crossing (02 and 05 keyed by moment; 05 already has active lanes). 03 gains the cache-down trace variant (same five hops, fourth throws, fifth answers). 05 gains a one-line bridge saying how the provider fix reached main (told in 04's hops today). 06 keeps the state panel on the map and repeated at the top of the drawer, and gets its own litmus question distinct from 05. One evidence component renders the drawer, the easy mistake, the 21 cards on 07, and the marker source-check notes. Optional 'here' override per chapter for details shared between scenes (client, image). Claim count follows the content, not lesson 01's three.
acceptance_criteria: Each lesson answers its litmus question from the page with the drawer closed; every claim has a headline under twelve words; the Easy mistake to What you can now say sequence is present; npm run check green; a second agent reviews before push.
notes: Lessons 02 (PR #5) and 03 (PR #6) merged 13 Sep 2026 via Keelson beads-work runs plus an orchestrator fix pass each. Remaining: 04, 05, 06 after the pilot; one evidence component; optional here override.

title: Navigation frame: Learn · Explore · Field guides, seven-lesson rail, position line
description: Masthead becomes Learn · Explore · Field guides (Listen leaves the masthead; the Listen route stays, reached from Start, the dock, and cue rows). Rail lists Start here and the seven lessons only: no subtitles, no book labels, no supplements. Position line 'Lesson n of 7 · book' above every headline; footer keeps Next. AGENTS.md 'the rail and the start page group by book' becomes 'the position line and the start page name the book'. Depends on the lesson 01 epic being judged in use.
acceptance_criteria: All routes unchanged; rail and masthead match the prototype; npm run check green.
notes: Assign to a Claude (Fable) coding peer in its own worktree, with the same brief shape used for Phase A, to compare against the Codex (gpt-6-astra) implementation of fn-5rl. Worktree needs its own Vite port: vite.config.js pins 5173/4173 with strictPort, so run npx vite --port 5174 --strictPort or build and serve dist elsewhere.
close_reason: Reviewer round 4 (13 Sep 2026): the LEARN-headed rail already establishes place; Explore · Listen · Field guides in the masthead works. Leave navigation alone rather than churn it. Reopen only if the pilot says learners are lost.
